definition: Cost–benefit analysis is a way of comparing an intervention’s expected benefits with its costs in economic terms. In mental health research, it can be used to judge whether treatments such as psychotherapy or medication are worth the resources they require.

reasons: The definition states a general meaning of “cost–benefit analysis” (comparing expected benefits with costs in economic terms). The provided packet does not contain any definition or explanation supporting this general characterization—only that a study “performed a cost-benefit analysis (CBA)” for specific treatments.

The definition’s mental-health-research usage claim (e.g., judging whether psychotherapy or medication are worth resources) is not explicitly supported by the packet text beyond the fact that CBA was applied to IPT and fluoxetine. No details are provided about the method or purpose of the comparison in the packet.

Because the packet lacks the substantive conceptual description required (the “way of comparing … benefits with costs in economic terms”), the definition cannot be verified as grounded in the supplied source.
